newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corp bond trading quiet, new issues dominate.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corp bond trading quiet, new issues dominate.

text.p: U.S. corporate high-grade bonds were up in line with U.S. Treasuries in relatively quiet trade as new issues once again dominated market activity, dealers said.
"All action is centered on these new issues," said one high-grade corporate trader. "All else remains quiet and stable on the secondary front."
Abbey National Plc's new perpetual note issue was seen tighter on the break at 76 basis points bid after pricing on Wednesday at a spread of 78 basis points, traders said.
"Abbey notes were tighter bid at 76 in the secondary market," one high-grade trader said.
Among other new issues, Campbell Soup's new 6.90 percent notes were seen trading at a spread of 35 basis points after initially tightening a touch at the break, dealers said.
"Players were bidding agrresively for the (Campbell) paper on the street," said one syndicate source. "It met with very good demand."
Meanwhile, new issues are expected to dominate activity as U.S. corporations capitalize on favorable interest rates to finance debt and paper hungry investors absorb the supply.
"Debt issues should continue to flow in as long as the demand for the paper is there...and recent supply has met with very good investor interest," said one high-grade syndicate source.
Meanwhile, traders said corporate spreads were unaffected by the recent bulk of supply and remained unchanged on the day.

Turning to secondary junk trade, news that Tenet Healthcare Corp had agreed to acquire OrNda HealthCorp for about $1.8 billion in a tax-free stock transaction sent the companies' bonds higher, traders said.
Tenet 10.125 percent paper gained a full point on the news to trade at 109-1/2 bid, 110 offer, while the company's 8.625 percent debt rose a 1/2 to traded at 105-1/4 bid, high-yield traders said.
Oranda Healthcare's 11-3/8 percent paper also traded up on the news gaining 3/4 of a point at 113 bid, they added.
Turning to the supermarket sector, paper was seen weaker with Grand Union and Ralphs Groceries' both trading off by 1/4 point, traders said.
In the government market, the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond was up 19/32 at 99-6/32 to yield 6.81 percent.
